de8_tests_it_fails.topic: Claimed models, corporate failures, succession, company-states

claims.text: Land p.6 (quoted passage): neocameralism 'has never been tried'; closest equivalents Frederick the Great and 'lost fragments of the British Empire such as Hong Kong, Singapore and Dubai'; 'weak only in political freedom, and political freedom is unimportant by definition when government is stable and effective'
Land p.5 (quoted passage): a state is 'a business which owns a country'; shares, one vote each, shareholders elect a board which hires and fires managers; residents are customers

Kofman (New Yorker 2025): Yarvin proposes a 'patchwork' of statelets 'like Singapore or Dubai'; a secret board can select and recall the CEO; board members would hold cryptographic keys able to disarm all government weapons to prevent a coup
Freedom House 2026: Singapore 48/100 Partly Free (PR 19/40, CL 29/60), dominated by the PAP and the Lee family since 1959
Freedom House 2026: UAE 18/100 Not Free (PR 5/40, CL 13/60); parties banned; all authority rests with the seven hereditary rulers
Geddes-Wright-Frantz 2014 typology: dominant party, military, personalist, monarchy, oligarchic, indirect military, hybrids
Tan (2009) describes Singapore as a hegemonic party autocracy with institutionalised, planned leadership succession in the PAP
Lawrence Wong became Singapore's fourth PM on 15 May 2024, succeeding Lee Hsien Loong (PM since 2004), chosen as PAP leader with unanimous backing of PAP MPs

Blattman, Gehlbach and Yu (NBER w34093): any autocratic growth penalty is concentrated in personalist regimes; institutionalised autocracies grow at rates statistically similar to democracies; 179 countries 1960-2010
Kostadinova and Neshkova (2025), 32 countries: personalist leaders associated with higher grand and petty corruption; time in power intensifies it
Kokkonen and Sundell (2014): risk of deposition several times higher in European monarchies without primogeniture, 1000-1800

Yarvin (CNN, 30 May 2025): monarchies 'don't generally see a Holocaust'; 'concentrate that power in a single individual and then just hope somehow that this is the right individual'; monarch accountable to a corporate board, not the citizen
John J. Ray III (FTX, 17 Nov 2022): never seen 'such a complete failure of corporate controls'; control concentrated in 'a very small group'; he had worked on Enron
Bankman-Fried convicted of seven counts (2023) and sentenced to 25 years on 28 March 2024 (Judge Kaplan); at least $8bn in customer funds taken
Enron collapsed in December 2001, then the largest US bankruptcy; Lay convicted on all six counts and Skilling on 19 of 28, 25 May 2006

Regulating Act 1773: Parliament's first intervention, prompted by the company's misgovernment of Bengal brought to a crisis by threatened bankruptcy and a loan request; raised shareholder vote qualification from £500 to £1,000
Government of India Act 1858 transferred most of the company's powers to the Crown
History Hit: Bengal famine 1769-70 death toll put at upwards of 10 million, worsened by company monopoly and taxation; 1857 rebellion; company dissolved by Act of Parliament 1873/1874

VOC chartered 20 March 1602 with powers to wage war, imprison and execute, make treaties, coin money, found colonies; Banda conquest 1609-1621 left about 1,000 of 15,000 inhabitants; board dismissed 1796; charter expired 31 Dec 1799, debts to Batavian Republic

Land p.5, summarising Moldbug: 'sovereignty cannot be eliminated, caged, or controlled'; 'divided powers flow back together'; constitutions have 'exactly as much real authority as a sovereign interpretative power allows them to have'
Land p.29 uses Singapore, Hong Kong, Taipei and Shanghai as cities where it is safe to walk at night

de8_who_enforces_the_charter.topic: Removing a bad CEO-sovereign: keys, exit, voice, checks

claims.text: Hirschman (1970) p.4: exit = customers stop buying or members leave; voice = members express dissatisfaction directly to management; p.43 'The presence of the exit alternative can therefore tend to atrophy the development of the art of voice'; p.46 the most quality-conscious exit first; where exit is unavailable voice is the only reaction

Federalist 51: 'Ambition must be made to counteract ambition'; 'If men were angels, no government would be necessary'; government must 'control the governed; and in the next place oblige it to control itself'; 'A dependence on the people is, no doubt, the primary control'

Compact (3 Nov 2025): under corporate law the CEO serves at the board's pleasure; a dominant shareholder could install loyalists and amend the constitution; exit is not guaranteed; the model is 'managerial democracy in corporate drag'
22nd Amendment, approved by Congress 1947, ratified 27 Feb 1951: 'No person shall be elected to the office of the President more than twice'; FDR had won a third term in 1940 and a fourth in 1944

Review summarising Patchwork: shareholders would have encryption keys giving access to the national military arsenal; the design is said to be stable only with modern cryptography (C, supports Kofman)
Urbit created by Yarvin, first code 2010, network launched 2013; Yarvin founded Tlon to build it; Thiel the most notable seed investor; Yarvin left Tlon in 2019

Article II s.4: President, Vice President and civil officers 'shall be removed from Office on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors'; House has sole power of impeachment, Senate sole power to try
